messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to decide packaging tradeoffs for the VPC/on‑prem path that lets customers manage networking themselves (peered VPCs, deterministic IPs) versus Redwood‑managed gateway. Target is Q3 launch criteria. Who's in?

ajay: In. Main constraints I see: IP preservation during upgrade, minimal downtime, and a clear handshake for peering. Also need to confirm support matrix for NATed setups vs. direct peering.

kevin: From runtime side: model artifacts + kernels vary by quantization and sequence-length optimizations. Rolling upgrades across variants are doable but we may need to dual-serve compatible artifacts for a short window. That implies ~<5% extra capacity during rollout if customers want zero-diff.

sarah-cs: Customers keep asking for deterministic outgoing IPs and the ability to manage their peering lifecycle. A few enterprise deals require a bounded upgrade window SLA. @maria can we separate "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" for sales?

olivia: Security note: we must preserve KMS/HSM bindings during any migration. Also audit log continuity is non-negotiable for compliance teams. If handshake includes cert exchange, include cert rotation/expiry handling in the plan.

ajay: Proposal: two shipping lanes — "Handshook" (customer-managed peering + deterministic IPs) and "Gateway" (Redwood-managed peering where we abstract network). Handshook = heavier field validation, longer validation cycle, premium pricing. Gateway = faster onboarding.

maria: Suggested launch criteria (draft):
```
1) End‑to‑end successful install with customer peering in staging (no manual network hacks)
2) Automated rollback path that achieves <15 min RTO for customer traffic
3) Audit logs and KMS bindings preserved across upgrade/migration
4) Clear operator checklist for netops (IP ranges, ASN, ports)
```
Agree / pushback?

kevin: Agree overall. Add: a preflight KV cache migration test so we don't break prefix-based inference cache. I can add a CLI check to installer: `kv-check --verify-prefixes` and a small shim to reconcile caches.

sarah-cs: :thumbsup: I'll capture three field customers for Early Access Program (EAP) and collect netops contact info. We should publish a one‑pager for customers that outlines required network primitives and expected rollback behavior.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: New draft playbook created by @ajay — /playbooks/handshake-packaging-v1 — https://redwood.internal/playbooks/handshake-packaging-v1

maria: Next steps: @ajay draft the gating checklist (include IP preservation test matrix), @kevin add the KV migration preflight, @olivia produce a security acceptance checklist, @sarah-cs nominate EAP customers and draft the customer one-pager. Sync back in 48h to finalize which lane we GA (Handshook vs Gateway). Thanks all!
